title: Faith in Prosperity vs. Adversity
english: Consider one slave who does not depart from his own master in a time of trial, tribulation, and flight; but those myriads of slaves who, in the time of trial and flight, abandon the master and withdraw. Are these slaves, who in prosperity abandon the master in the time of trial, able to be like those who follow the master in adversity? Not at all.

Peter believed, but seeing the dead raised and beholding his glory, he believed; Paul believed, but seeing light from heaven, which scorched the bodily eyes and enlightened the spiritual eyes; Abraham believed, but beholding a divine vision; Isaiah believed, but seeing him sitting upon a high throne and the Cherubim around him. All saw, but in glory; but this one in insolence; therefore he also cried out, 'Remember me, Lord, when you come in your kingdom' (Luke 23:42).

From those concerning me, you owe it to me to say: 'Why do you say?' That I am a sinner, and a murderer, and a robber until this hour; many are my evils, I confess, but I have in my mind a hidden faith, which no one knew, except the Master alone who suffers with me. From the outside, the Master holds the outward symbols of suffering; and I, he says, did not pay attention to the apparent insolence, but I glorify the hidden kingdom. So also you say: 'Lord, do not see my apparent injustices, but the hidden faith, and, Remember me, when you come in your kingdom' (Luke 23:42).

Christ, having said nothing to anyone, but being silent, neither answering Pilate nor any other ignorant soul of the Jews, answers then; and since it was very heavy and absurd to remain silent, he answers at last and says to the robber: 'Amen, amen, I say to you: today you will be with me in Paradise' (Luke 23:43). Oh, the goodness of the benefactor! Since I would ask for grace with delay, and you say, 'Remember me, Lord, when you come in your kingdom' (Luke 23:42).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Promise of Paradise to the Thief
english: “You asked for a slow thing, but I give a swift grace; today you shall be with me in paradise.” Have you seen the salvation of God? Have you seen the benevolence of the Lord? Have you seen the great judge of the truth? “Today you shall be with me in paradise.” Before this, no one among the Jews or the patriarchs heard the promise of paradise from the time that Adam passed through and went out of it; even though God promised ten thousand things to the faithful humans; yet He promised paradise to no one, not even to the thief. Nowhere does the mouth of God appear promising paradise to man after Adam was cast out, or even to this one, the thief first.

Why did He not first say something about paradise to any of the patriarchs, or any of the prophets, or any of the apostles? But to the ancients He promised: “I will give you a land flowing with milk and honey” (Exodus 3:8); to the apostles He says: “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven” (Matthew 5:3); paradise is nowhere; He keeps the paradise in the midst as a promise first to the thief. For when Paul says: “I was caught up into paradise” (2 Corinthians 12:4); but this happened after the thief.

Why then did he enter first, having cried out with one voice? For why? Often he sang psalms; often he struggled; often he glorified God; once, he says, “my God is righteous, the victor of salvation”; since He did not cast out the first man Adam from paradise because of many sins, but because of one disobedience; so the yoke of righteousness promised to let the thief enter into paradise first, not having confessed many things, but having brought forward one confession of faith. It is said of Adam's sin, that he touched the tree contrary to the commandment; what is the justification of the thief? That he touched the cross with faith, and entered into paradise. title: The Baptism of the Thief
english: The thief was given the opportunity to believe and be enlightened, for the Savior had decreed: 'Unless one is born of water and Spirit, he shall certainly not enter the kingdom of heaven' (John 3:5). The thief found no opportunity or boldness, nor did he have the time to be baptized, for he was hanging on the cross.

The Savior finds a way even in a desperate way. Since the one aged by sins had believed in the Savior, and he needed to be cleansed, Christ manages, after the passion, that the soldier pierce the side of the Lord with a spear, and blood and water gush out; for from his side, the Evangelist says, 'Blood and water came out' (John 19:34), in the truth of the one fallen, as a type of the mysteries. And the blood and water did not come out simply flowing, but in a torrent, so that it might sprinkle the body of the thief; for that which is sent in a torrent sprinkles, but that which flows simply flows calmly, as it comes. But in a torrent blood and water came out from the side, so that, having sprinkled the thief, it might baptize him, as the Apostle says: 'We have come to Zion with the blood of sprinkling, speaking better than Abel' (Hebrews 12:24).

Why does the blood of Christ speak better than Abel? Because the blood of Abel was at the peak of the murderer, but the blood of Christ cleanses even the murderers who repent. Learn therefore the zeal for the truth, and love the boldness for the sake of Christ; follow the true Teacher struggling for the truth, so that having heard thus from the Apostle Paul, 'Become imitators of me, as I am of Christ' (1 Cor 11:1), you may be worthy yourself of the crowns of righteousness, which Christ our God has prepared for the eternal good things for those who loved him (2 Tim 4:8); of which may we all attain, by the grace and philanthropy of our Lord Jesus Christ, to whom belongs the glory and the power, now and always, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
